identity.name: West Ukrainian People's Republic
alt_names: Western Oblast of the Ukrainian People's Republic

land.text: Eastern Galicia: the republic 'controlled most of Eastern Galicia from November 1918 to July 1919'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Austria-Hungary and the Kingdom of Galicia and Lodomeria'. kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria records the loss on 19 October 1918 (its /ledger/8) and austria-hungary hands the land over in its /ledger/34; the republic was proclaimed on 1 November.

land.text: the eastern lands of the monarchy; the republic also claimed northern Bukovina and Carpathian Ruthenia but held neither

predecessors.note: The austria-hungary dossier's land for this state (its /ledger/34) is the Ukrainian cells of the 1912 outline without Transcarpathia and Bukovina; this dossier draws the Eastern Galicia region named on the page.

land.text: the republic, which 'became the Western Oblast of the UPR' with the Unification Act of 22 January 1919; Lviv had been Polish since 21 November 1918

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: the Ukrainian People's Republic, Second Polish Republic, First Czechoslovak Republic and Kingdom of Romania' (the last three took the claimed lands later). The ukrainian-people-s-republic dossier records the union as a merge (its /ledger/10) and the loss of Eastern Galicia to Poland on 18 July 1919.

capitals.name: Lviv (Lemberg, Lwow)
capitals.note: 1 November to 21 November 1918, when Polish forces took the city.

capitals.name: Stanyslaviv (Ivano-Frankivsk)
capitals.note: Capital 'until 26 May 1919' on the page, beyond the merger of January 1919 that ends this dossier.

correction.text: Eastern Galicia, 'most of' which the republic controlled; the republic claimed northern Bukovina and Carpathian Ruthenia as well

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row; the area sits in its Austria-Hungary 1912 shape and in the UPR 1919 shape). The page gives no area; it gives about 4 million people governed and 5.4 million in the claimed territory by the 1910 census. The gazetteer region resolves to about 50,000 km2, close to the 46,000 km2 of the Ukrainian cells of the Austro-Hungarian outline without Transcarpathia and Bukovina that austria-hungary hands over. Lviv is taken out by a ledger event on 21 November 1918.

ledger.note: 1 November 1918: the West Ukrainian People's Republic is proclaimed at Lviv. 'The West Ukrainian People's Republic was proclaimed on 1 November 1918' (the National Rada had planned 3 November); 'Until November 13, 1918, the state was officially known as the Ukrainian State'; it 'controlled most of Eastern Galicia from November 1918 to July 1919'.

region.text: Eastern Galicia, including Lviv and the Drohobych oil fields

ledger.note: 1 November 1918: the Polish-Ukrainian War breaks out in Lviv. 'on 1st November 1918 the Polish-Ukrainian war of Eastern Galicia broke out'; Polish forces tried to seize the Drohobych oil fields on 9 November and were driven back (WUPR page); 'The Ukrainians retained control over the oil fields until May 1919'. second-polish-republic records this contest against ukrainian-people-s-republic.

region.text: Lviv, taken by Polish forces on 21 November 1918

ledger.note: 21 November 1918: Lviv falls to the Poles. The WUPR page: Lviv was the capital 'from 1 November until its loss to Polish forces on 21 November 1918'; the Polish-Ukrainian War page: Polish troops 'broke through the Ukrainian siege on November 21 and arrived in the city'. second-polish-republic has no matching gain.
21 November 1918: the government leaves Lviv for Ternopil, the capital 'until late December 1918' on the WUPR page (the page does not date the move itself).
Late December 1918: the capital moves from Ternopil to Stanyslaviv (Ivano-Frankivsk), the capital 'until 26 May 1919' (WUPR page; the move date is bridged from 'until late December').

region.text: Eastern Galicia without Lviv, united with the Ukrainian People's Republic

ledger.note: 22 January 1919: the Unification Act. 'The Unification Act with the Ukrainian People's Republic was signed on 22 January 1919. The republic became the Western Oblast of the UPR.' The exile government dropped the Act on 20 December 1919 and resumed the name in 1920.

region.text: Eastern Galicia, including Lviv and the Drohobych oil fields

ledger.note: 22 January 1919: this record closes with the state, not with the war. The fighting goes on in the ukrainian-people-s-republic record: the Ukrainians were 'pushed back to the line of the Zbruch river on 16-18 July' and 'Poland won the disputed territory on 18 July 1919'.

region.text: the republic, merged into the Ukrainian People's Republic as its Western Oblast

ledger.note: 22 January 1919: the West Ukrainian People's Republic ends as a separate state. The page keeps a Western Oblast, the Ukrainian Galician Army and the Stanyslaviv government until the retreat across the Zbruch on 16 July 1919, and an exile government in Vienna to 15 March 1923.

wars.name: Polish-Ukrainian War

zones.text: Eastern Galicia, including Lviv and the Drohobych oil fields

wars.outcome: Fighting began in Lviv on 1 November 1918; the Poles took Lviv on 21 November, the Ukrainians reached Przemysl's outer defences on 9 December and were forced back by 17 December, advanced 120 km along the Dniester by 27 June 1919 (the Chortkiv offensive) and were pushed back to the Zbruch on 16-18 July; 'Poland won the disputed territory on 18 July 1919'.
wars.note: The WUPR dossier ends on 22 January 1919 with the union with the UPR; the rest of the war is in ukrainian-people-s-republic and second-polish-republic. The Allied Council legitimised Polish control on 25 June 1919 and the Council of Ambassadors incorporated Galicia into Poland on 14 March 1923.

certainty.note: A war front that moved from week to week; no treaty line. The republic held 'most of' Eastern Galicia and claimed northern Bukovina and Carpathian Ruthenia, which it never held (Bukovina: a Ukrainian polity proclaimed on 6 November 1918 and dissolved on 11 November when the Romanian Army occupied Chernivtsi).

notes: Written 2026-11-01 for batch g-eu-b (2 pages opened; budget 2-5). New dossier: Cliopatria has no row for the republic. THE STATE: the Ukrainian state of Eastern Galicia, 1 November 1918 to its union with the UPR on 22 January 1919, drawn as the Eastern Galicia region (about 50,000 km2). NOT SETTLED: (1) the end: the page and the ukrainian-people-s-republic dossier treat the union of 22 January 1919 as the end of a separate state, but the Western Oblast, the Ukrainian Galician Army and the Stanyslaviv government lasted to July 1919, and an exile government kept the name to 15 March 1923; the dossier ends at the union so the cells are not drawn twice; (2) second-polish-republic records the Eastern Galicia contest (1 November 1918 to 18 July 1919) and the final gain against ukrainian-people-s-republic; until 22 January 1919 the counterpart should be west-ukrainian-people-s-republic, and a gain of Lviv on 21 November 1918 is missing there; (3) the contest_end here closes the record with the state, not the war (a bridge, confidence 1); (4) the page dates the republic 1 November 1918 but cites a proclamation of 19 October 1918 without discussing it; kingdom-of-galicia-and-lodomeria and austria-hungary use October 1918 for the same hand-over; (5) the Polish-Ukrainian War page's infobox gives the Bukovyna Viche the dates 6-11 November 1919 against its text's 1918; (6) small polities named on the pages with no dossier: the Lemko-Rusyn Republic (declared 5 December 1918, against union with the republic) and the Komancza Republic (4 November 1918 to 23 January 1919, suppressed by Poland) in Lemkivshchyna, the Bukovyna Viche (6-11 November 1918); (7) no ruler strip: the page names Yevhen Petrushevych as chairman of the National Council and president, with no years; (8) wikidata null (not read from a page).
